title: QB9_G Q6 and Q3 - the Treaty/Convention/Protocol legal hierarchy removed, and the instrument-title-is-not-a-rank model rebuilt on VCLT, UN Treaty Collection and IMO authority
rationale: The Founder, studying from the MIW study roadmap, reported that QB9_G Q6 taught a legal hierarchy - Treaty, then Convention, then Protocol - printed under the card's own "Hierarchy" heading. Verified against the primary text of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969, read from the ILC/UN text. Article 2(1)(a) defines a treaty as "an international agreement concluded between States in written form and governed by international law, whether embodied in a single instrument or in two or more related instruments and whatever its particular designation". The closing qualifier settles the question: an instrument's designation does not determine its legal status, so "Convention" and "Protocol" are treaty titles reflecting practice, not tiers, and there is no ranking to teach. Three further defects travelled with the hierarchy in the same card. (1) A Protocol was defined as one that "amends or structurally updates an existing Convention"; the UN Treaty Collection records protocols of signature, optional protocols, protocols based on a framework treaty, protocols to amend, protocols as a supplementary treaty and proces-verbaux, so a protocol is not by definition an amendment. (2) The card stated as a universal that a Protocol "needs its own separate ratification", and that a State generally cannot join a Protocol without ratifying the parent; both are false, and the card's own flagship example disproves the first - MARPOL Protocol of 1978, Art.IV(1), lets a State become a Party by signature without reservation as to ratification, acceptance or approval, by signature followed by that act, or by accession, and imposes no prior-ratification condition, while the MARPOL Protocol of 1997, Art.5(1), is the opposite case, open only to Contracting States to the 1978 Protocol. VCLT Art.11 is the governing rule and the instrument's own final clauses control. (3) The card said an IMO Resolution is "committee guidance without independent treaty force"; amendments to the SOLAS annex are adopted BY MSC resolution under SOLAS Art.VIII(b) and bind Contracting Governments through tacit acceptance, resolution MSC.48(66) adopted the LSA Code and MSC.47(66) adopted the SOLAS chapter III amendments that made it mandatory on or after 1 July 1998, and only some resolutions stay recommendatory. Q6 was rebuilt with the official definition presented first and the MIW plain-language memory line separated and explicitly labelled as MIW's own wording. Q3 carried the same resolution defect in its instrument ladder - "Guideline, circular or resolution - recommendatory" - and additionally gave MARPOL's 1978 Protocol as an example of a State being party to a parent convention but not its protocol, which is the one instrument for which that cannot be true, because the 1973 Convention never entered into force alone. Both were corrected and Q3 now states that its ladder ranks instruments by what makes them binding, not by legal class.
note: Every date and citation in the rebuilt card was verified against a primary or first-party source and none was inherited from the previous version: VCLT adopted 22 May 1969 and in force 27 January 1980 (UN Treaty Collection status page); MARPOL Convention adopted 2 November 1973, not in force alone, absorbed by the 1978 Protocol, combined instrument in force 2 October 1983, Annex VI in force 19 May 2005 (IMO MARPOL page); MARPOL Protocol of 1978 Art.I(1), I(2) and IV(1) and MARPOL Protocol of 1997 Art.5(1) and its adoption at London on 26 September 1997 (the Protocol texts themselves); SOLAS Protocol of 1988 adopted 11 November 1988 and in force 3 February 2000, introducing the HSSC with the 1988 Load Lines Protocol (IMO HSSC page); LLMC Protocol of 1996 adopted 2 May 1996, in force 13 May 2004, raising the 1976 limits and introducing tacit acceptance for updating them (IMO LLMC page); resolution MSC.48(66) adopted 4 June 1996 adopting the LSA Code and recording MSC.47(66) as making it mandatory on or after 1 July 1998 (the resolution text). A bank-wide definition and legal-terminology audit was run over all 86 question-bearing pages and 38 cheat sheets before this record was written. Inside the Oral QB the hierarchy, the universal-ratification claim and the resolution claim were confined to QB9_G and its cheat sheet. Statements elsewhere that pattern-match the same wording were read in context and are CORRECT because they are scoped to a named instrument, and were deliberately not changed: QB1_A Q25 on A.987(24), QB2_G Q1 on the 2011 TDC Code under A.1048(27), QB5_D Q3 on the IMO/ILO harassment guidelines and A.1147(31), and QB9_G Q3's own Code rung. An independent clean-context review of the rebuilt card found seven further items, all fixed before this record was written, of which the two material ones were that the block headed "Official terminology (UN Treaty Collection)" carried MIW's own gloss - "has the same legal characteristics as a treaty" - while omitting the source's actual opening sentence, that a protocol is "used for agreements less formal than those entitled 'treaty' or 'convention'"; and the Q3 MARPOL 1978 example above. The first is the same defect class this correction exists to remove, reproduced by the fix, and is why the UNTC block now quotes the source and labels the reading that follows it as MIW's. Outside the Oral QB the same legal defect is live in four other governed pipelines and was verified but deliberately held: it is registered as OPEN-G1-014 to OPEN-G1-018 in meoclass1/oral-intelligence/examiner-audit/AUGUST2026_OPEN_ITEMS.json with a line-level inventory. OPEN-G1-014, the current framework answer CA-EM-0003, contradicts the corrected Q6 head-on on the same question and is the highest priority. A SECOND independent clean-context review, run over the fixes rather than over the original card, returned FAIL and found a further eight items, all fixed before this record was written. The material finding was a single unrepaired seam: the doctrinal bodies of Q6 and Q3 had been corrected while the SUMMARY surfaces still taught the pre-edit model. Q3's 15-second and 60-second answers still presented ratification, acceptance, approval and accession as a closed set of four with identical effect; Q3's reg-box attributed that closed set to VCLT Art.11, which does not define those terms at all (Art.2(1)(b) does) and does not close the list; and the cheat sheet's Q548 flip-card said "Signature -> Ratification/Acceptance/Approval/Accession (all equal legal effect)", so the same sheet's two flip-cards taught opposite things. That is worse than the uncorrected state, because the card would have argued with itself in front of an examiner. All are now corrected. The same pass also found that the cheat-sheet diagram caption written earlier in this correction described a Protocol that the diagram does not contain - the SVG is the convention-adoption pipeline and has no Protocol node - so the caption now describes the diagram and points at the Convention vs Protocol confusable pair instead. Three smaller items were fixed: the Q3 ladder still narrowed a Protocol to one that "modifies or supplements" a convention, where Q6 forbids the amendment-only reading; the VCLT Art.2(1)(a) quotation was closed with a full stop where the article has a semicolon and omitted the paragraph numeral, which matters in a card about quotation fidelity; and an em dash was used as a numeric range separator in "1976-77". The review additionally reported that both timed answers were roughly twice their stated budget, citing 51 and 115 words. Those figures were checked against the live corpus and are its 25th percentile, not a ceiling: across 132 15-second and 130 60-second answers the medians are 67 and 156. The answers were trimmed anyway, from 102 to 59 and from 226 to 166, which places both near the corpus median rather than at its tail. Future sessions should not treat 51/115 as a limit.

artefacts.rationale: Carries no q-card, so it takes no digest, but it held FOUR candidate-facing copies of the affected model, and candidates memorise a cheat sheet before they read a card. All four were reconciled. The "Confusable Pair: Convention vs Protocol" box said a Protocol "is a separate instrument needing its own ratification". The Q554 flip-card answer said "Treaty = umbrella legal term ... Protocol = major structural add-on/update, same binding force, own ratification". The Q548 flip-card answer - found only by the SECOND independent review, because the first pass fixed the Convention-vs-Protocol material and did not look at the adoption card on the same sheet - said "Signature -> Ratification/Acceptance/Approval/Accession (all equal legal effect)", which left the sheet's two flip-cards teaching opposite things about the same list. And the concept-map diagram caption said a Protocol "is a structural add-on anywhere in this chain that needs its own separate ratification"; its first replacement in this correction was itself defective, describing a Protocol that the diagram does not contain, and it now describes the adoption pipeline the SVG actually draws and points at the confusable pair below for the Protocol distinction. The SVG itself was not edited: its "Ratify / Accept / Approve / Accede" node is a stage label in an adoption flow rather than a claim that those four are the only routes, the claim having lived in the flip-card text that has now been corrected, and its coordinates are fixed so re-labelling it risks overflow. That node is recorded here so a later session does not read its absence from this correction as an oversight.

cards.rationale: The card the Founder reported. Every surface of it carried the defective model and all were rebuilt: the 15-Second answer, the 60-Second answer, the "Hierarchy" heading and its block, the Key examples list, the Trap point, the reg-box, the CE Oral Tip and four of the five deep-dives. The "Hierarchy" heading is deleted outright rather than reworded, because the heading itself was the claim. New blocks give the VCLT Art.2(1)(a) definition with its chapeau and a scope note under VCLT Art.3, the UN Treaty Collection terminology for Convention and Protocol quoted rather than paraphrased, a consent-to-be-bound block built on VCLT Art.11 with the MARPOL 1978 and 1997 Protocols as the two opposite worked cases, a verified maritime examples list, and a block on where an IMO Resolution fits. The MIW memory line survives but under a heading that says it is MIW wording and not an official definition, and it now names the old ladder only to forbid it. The 15-Second answer was cut from 102 words to 59 and the 60-Second answer from 226 to 166, both back inside the corpus's own distribution. Question text, anchor and card position are unchanged. Version badge Q6 v1.0 -> v1.1. Two further quotation-fidelity items were fixed after the second review: the VCLT Art.2(1)(a) quotation now carries the paragraph numeral and the article's own terminal semicolon, with a bracketed note that sub-paragraphs (b) to (j) follow, rather than being presented as a closed sentence ending in a full stop; and an em dash used as a numeric range separator in "1976-77" is now an en dash.

The same resolution defect, on the neighbouring card. Q3's instrument ladder read "Guideline, circular or resolution - recommendatory", lumping a resolution with instruments that are genuinely recommendatory. That rung is now split: guideline and circular keep the recommendatory rung, and a new Resolution entry states that a resolution is the vehicle rather than a rung, that MSC and MEPC resolutions are how SOLAS and MARPOL annex amendments are adopted and bind through tacit acceptance, that MSC.48(66) adopted the LSA Code which SOLAS chapter III then made mandatory, and that only some resolutions stay recommendatory. Two further defects were found in Q3 by independent review while checking it against Q6 and were corrected in the same pass. Its Protocol bullet gave "MARPOL's 1978 and 1997 Protocols" as standard examples of a State being party to a parent convention but not to its protocol; the 1978 Protocol is the one instrument for which that cannot be true, since the 1973 Convention never entered into force by itself and a State joins the combined MARPOL 73/78 through the Protocol, so the example is now the 1997 MARPOL Protocol and the 1988 SOLAS and Load Line Protocols, with the 1978 Protocol named explicitly as not being one of them. And its ratification block presented ratification, acceptance, approval and accession as a closed set, which is the narrower rule Q6's trap point exists to defeat; it now records that VCLT Art.11 also allows signature alone, exchange of instruments and any other agreed means, and that the instrument's own final clauses decide. The ladder's introduction now states that it ranks instruments by what makes them binding on you and not by legal class, and cross-refers to Q6, so the word "ladder" cannot be read as a legal hierarchy. Version badge Q3 v1.0 -> v1.1. A second independent review then found that Q3's own summary surfaces had not been carried through with its body. Its 15-second and 60-second answers still taught ratification, acceptance, approval and accession as a closed set of four of identical effect, which is the narrower rule the body three paragraphs below now denies; both were rewritten to say that consent is expressed by whichever means the instrument's final clauses allow. Its reg-box row read 'Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969, Art.11 - Defines ratification/acceptance/approval/accession as equivalent means of consent', which is wrong twice over: Art.11 lists means and does not define those acts, Art.2(1)(b) defines them, and the row re-asserted the closed list. It is now two rows, Art.2(1)(b) for the definitions and Art.11 for the open list of means. The ladder's Protocol rung still said a Protocol 'modifies or supplements' a convention, omitting the implementing and optional protocols that Q6 adds precisely to defeat the amendment-only reading, and now carries all four verbs. One STRUCTURAL defect was also repaired, and it PRE-DATES this correction: the entire instrument-ladder block - its h4, its introductory paragraph, its seven-item list and its closing paragraph - sat OUTSIDE <div class="answer-body">, having been appended after that div closed when the ladder was added by enrichment action A046. It was the only such block in the file; the other seven cards keep every heading and paragraph inside answer-body. Div balance was correct, so nothing failed - the block simply lost the .answer-body typography and rendered in a different typeface and size from the rest of the answer. The closing div was moved to after the ladder, and all seven cards now report zero headings outside answer-body. This is a SCOPE_PASS defect found by the same sweep, not a regression introduced here.
